chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Amr from Jamil from Aban from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).
That he was asked about a man who bequeathed something unspecified, so he said: 'The unspecified thing in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) is one of six.'

key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the book of Ali (referring to a specific juristic text)

ai.seo_question: What are the six categories of an unspecified bequest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on ambiguous bequests (al-wasiyya al-mubhama) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam highlights the juristic reliance on the 'Book of Ali' (Kitab Ali), a foundational source of fiqh often identified with the lost *Kitab al-Jami* or early legal rulings attributed to Imam Ali. It establishes that unspecified bequests are not left to arbitrary interpretation but are systematically categorized into six distinct legal scenarios, reflecting the precision of Shia jurisprudence in handling testamentary ambiguity.
